(4) Fish Population of the River
About 39 species of fishes have been observed or are expected to be in the Susquehanna near Harrisburg. These include many species of game and pan fishes, including Muskellunge (Esox Masquinongy), northern pike (Esox Lucius), walleye (Stizastedion Vitoreum Vitreum), largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, crappies, and other fishes belonging to the sunfish family, which have been taken in trophy size in the Harrisburg area. Species other than those listed may be taken but not in significant numbers.
During numerous visits to the project area in May of 1973, no one was observed fishing in the River. However, it is not uncommon for persons working and living in the area to fish the river during the summer months, especially during their lunch periods.
h. The Economy
The economy of the City of Harrisburg and the Harrisburg SMSA appears to be generally strong as indicated by a number of statistical reports developed by various sources. The economic base of the area is best expressed by employment figures as they relate to the various sources of employment. An examination of Table 5 below indicates a very diversified economic area with the strongest types of employment being those of manufacturing, wholesale and retail trade, professional and related services, and public administration.
A futher analysis of the types of occupations filling these jobs indicates a large relative percentage of clerical or white collar workers (See Table 6 below). Other statistical information furnished in census reports over the last few decades demonstrates a marked trend away from the manufacturing sector. Other factors and trends are the relative by strong use of the service sectors and steady increase in the retail and finance, insurance, etc., sectors of employment.
The relatively high percentage of clerical workers, especially in the City of Harrisburg, may be due in part to the fact that Harrisburg is the capital of the Commonwealth and many of the State agencies are located within the City.
